Conversation A

YOUR SIDE: We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording. 1. **Purpose and access.** The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to plan, perform and report the agreed actuator vibration tests. Before access, the parties must approve in writing a list of named test personnel and their roles. Each person, including any external adviser, must need access for that role and be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The same approval applies to replacements. The Testing House remains responsible for their compliance. 2. **Working copies and fixtures.** Named personnel may make only the working copies reasonably needed for the tests. Digital copies must be encrypted in transit and at rest and accessible only to named personnel. The Testing House may derive only the geometry needed to design and fabricate test fixtures and may use those fixtures only for these tests. Neither the source material nor any derived geometry or fixture may be used to develop a competing product. 3. **Destruction and verification.** Within 15 business days after the Design Owner’s written acceptance of the final test report, or earlier termination of the test engagement, the Testing House must securely erase the supplied drawings, CAD files, working copies and derived fixture files, destroy the physical derivative fixtures, and obtain confirmation from any approved external recipient that it has done the same. Within that period, the Testing House must provide a written certificate from an independent verifier identifying the materials covered, the destruction methods and the completion dates. That certificate satisfies the verification requirement without site access by the Design Owner. The Testing House may retain test results and a final report free of sensitive geometry. Would naming an external fixture machinist before fabrication meet your staffing needs? If a backup cycle or test-record retention obligation makes the destruction period impracticable, please identify the specific material and minimum retention period so we can agree wording for it. COUNTERPARTY: Much of your draft works for us. We accept the purpose limit, the encryption and working-copy rules, the fixture-use restriction, the non-compete use bar, and verification without site access. Three points need changes. **1. External recipients and substitution.** Naming the machinist before fabrication works, but there are two external recipients: a specialist machining shop for fixtures and an accredited lab for part of the testing. Clause 1 as drafted also has no route for replacing either mid-job without a fresh approval that could stall the test schedule. We propose adding to clause 1: > "The approved list will identify each external recipient by entity and role. External recipients receive only isolated drawing extracts limited to the geometry needed for their task, not the full drawing set or CAD model. If an external recipient or named individual must be replaced during the engagement, the Testing House will give written notice identifying the replacement and its role. The Design Owner may object on reasonable grounds within 3 business days; absent objection, the replacement is approved. No material is released to the replacement until that period ends and it is bound by the required confidentiality terms." If 3 business days is too short for you, what period could you commit to? **2. Verification.** We can't accept an independent verifier as the only route. It adds cost and brings a third party onto a site shared with other customers. We propose replacing the certificate sentence in clause 3 with: > "Within that period, the Testing House must provide a written attestation signed by an authorised officer identifying the materials covered, the destruction methods and the completion dates, together with the written confirmations from each approved external recipient. That attestation satisfies the verification requirement. If the Design Owner has reasonable grounds to doubt its accuracy, the parties will agree a document-based review, or a visit scheduled on at least 10 business days' notice, limited to areas and systems holding the Design Owner's material and subject to the site's confidentiality obligations to other customers." This gives you a named, accountable signatory and a scheduled escalation path, but no unannounced access. **3. Retention.** The specific item is calibration records for the test equipment and set-up, which we must keep for two years. We propose replacing the last sentence of clause 3 with: > "The Testing House may retain test results, the final report, and calibration and test-set-up records for two years after completion of the tests, or longer where its accreditation requires, provided the retained records contain no drawings, CAD data or derived geometry. Retained records remain subject to the confidentiality and use restrictions of this agreement." Because those records carry no geometry, no carve-out from the 15-business-day destruction period is needed for the drawings, extracts or fixture files. Verification.** Yes. We accept an authorised officer’s attestation with the external recipients’ written confirmations as routine proof of destruction. Opening and deputy coverage.** The desk will take submissions on four fixed days each week beginning December 1, 2026. Finch is responsible for appointing the deputy and will identify the editor for recused matters in writing at signing. Before opening, Noor and the deputy will document the fourth-day procedure. During Noor’s three-day schedule, the deputy will acknowledge and log incoming submissions on the fourth day, triage them under the written criteria, and flag urgent matters to the duty editor that day. The deputy has no authority to decide corrections. Noor will train the deputy during scheduled Finch days and review the log and substantive recommendations on the next scheduled Finch day. Noor has no fourth-day on-call duty. **4. Intellectual property and outside-project carve-out.** Finch owns work Noor creates for the methods desk on Finch time. Noor may continue directing the existing editorial project identified in the disclosure under clause 5 until that project finishes. The outside project and its materials, including its data, drafts and unfinished articles, are expressly excluded from every Finch intellectual-property assignment, license and work-product provision applicable to this appointment. Those materials remain with the project. Finch acquires no ownership or license in them under this agreement. This carve-out controls over any inconsistent standard Finch provision. **5. Disclosure and recusal.** At signing, Noor will disclose in writing the outside project’s scope, funders and collaborators and will update the disclosure when they change. Noor will keep the two projects’ materials separate and will use no Finch resources or confidential submissions for the outside project. Noor will recuse from any Finch submission or correction involving the project, its data or its collaborators. The named Finch editor will handle that matter independently and exercise Noor’s authority under Schedule A throughout. **6. Editorial authority and review.** The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority subject to Schedule A, which forms part of this agreement. Nine months after the appointment begins, Finch and Noor will review desk performance, workload, time commitment, scope of the role and the operation of Schedule A. The review will cover the number of disputes and referrals, every referee outcome, every departure from a desk finding, and every decision to redact, defer or decline publication and its grounds. ## Schedule A — Methods corrections 1. **Standing authority.** Noor may determine whether a routine methods correction is warranted, settle its wording and clear it for publication. An author’s or editor’s objection alone does not suspend that authority. Finch retains control of acceptance decisions, scheduling, non-methods corrections and the non-methods elements of notices, subject to the publication deadlines below. 2. **Record and referral back.** When a methods correction is disputed, Noor will document the finding, supporting evidence and proposed wording. The editor-in-chief has five working days after receiving that record to refer the matter back to Noor once, giving specific written reasons. The author’s response may be included. If no referral is made within that period, the correction proceeds as cleared. 3. **Reconsideration and new evidence.** Noor will consider the referral in good faith and issue the desk’s final written finding and proposed wording within five working days, sooner if delay risks misleading readers. At any stage before publication, material new evidence must go to the desk first. Noor must consider it and reissue, revise or withdraw the finding before publication proceeds. 4. **Independent methods review.** Finch and Noor will jointly select an independent methods referee in advance. If the editor-in-chief still disputes the methods substance after reconsideration, they must identify the precise disputed claim and refer it with the full record within five working days of receiving Noor’s decision. Otherwise the correction proceeds as cleared. The referee will report to both parties within ten working days of referral. The ruling binds both parties on the accuracy of the disputed methods claim on the record reviewed. If the referee finds against the desk, Noor will withdraw or revise the statement accordingly. No correction will run on a claim the referee finds inaccurate. 5. **Publication after an upheld finding.** Finch will ordinarily publish the upheld methods statement on the article in Noor’s words within five working days of the ruling. The editor-in-chief authorizes the notice and controls its framing, context, placement and non-methods content. They may add a signed statement of their own. Finch may not substitute a contrary methods finding on the same record or attribute revised wording to the desk without Noor’s approval. 6. **Grounds and decision on publication.** The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority within the grounds agreed here. A decision to decline requires harm independent of the methods question. Permitted grounds are documented legal advice or a serious risk to the safety, privacy or confidentiality of an identifiable person or source. Disagreement with the finding and reputational consequences to the authors or Finch from an accurate correction are excluded as grounds. If the editor-in-chief declines, they must give Noor and the referee a signed decision within the same five-working-day period identifying the specific harm and explaining why it persists in light of the ruling. Documented legal review may extend that deadline once by up to ten working days. 7. **Redaction or delay.** Where redaction or delay can cure a permitted ground, the editor-in-chief will redact or defer rather than decline and will publish once the ground no longer applies. Noor will clear any redaction that changes the desk’s methods wording. The editor-in-chief will document the ground for redaction or deferral and give the reasons to Noor. 8. **Independent publication.** Any decision by Finch to decline publication triggers Noor’s right to publish the finding and its reasoning independently, in Noor’s words and identified as the Methods Desk’s finding, without further Finch editorial approval. In exercising that right, Noor will preserve confidential submission materials and third-party rights. For recused matters, the named editor takes Noor’s place throughout this schedule. YOUR SIDE: **Appointment letter — Methods Editor, Finch Review** Dear Noor, Finch Review confirms your appointment as Methods Editor on the following terms. **Schedule and compensation** Through February 2027, your fixed Finch days will be Monday through Wednesday. Your annual salary rate will be $75,000, prorated from a five-day, full-time base of $125,000. The deputy will cover Thursday intake through February, acknowledge submissions, log open cases and refer urgent matters directly to the editor-in-chief. The editor-in-chief may post an interim notice on a deputy-covered Thursday if an urgent concern needs attention before your return. You will train the deputy. Before launch, you and the deputy will document the procedures for intake, urgent referrals and handoffs on paid Finch time. You will review each Thursday’s log on your next scheduled Finch day and use it to coach the deputy during paid desk time. In late February, you and Finch will use the log to review submission volume, turnaround, workload and training needs. The March schedule and salary increase take effect regardless of the review’s outcome. **Methods corrections** You have final say over the desk’s methods assessment and the wording of its recommendation, subject to the recusal provision below. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority. The following procedures govern how you exercise standing authority and how Finch resolves disputes. 1. **Factual corrections.** When the reporting record establishes both an error in a published methods statement and the replacement wording, you may send the handling editor the supporting record and your proposed correction. This procedure covers errors such as a misstated sample size, an incorrect denominator or a description of a procedure that differs from the one used. The handling editor may object, or the editor-in-chief may place a hold, by the end of the next desk day. An objection or hold must identify the disputed fact or wording. If neither is raised by the deadline, you may publish the correction as drafted under standing authorization. 2. **Independent review.** Before launch, you and Finch will jointly select an independent methods editor. Upon a timely objection or hold, the reviewer will hear both editors and determine whether the reporting record establishes both the error and your proposed replacement. The reviewer’s finding is final for the desk’s factual assessment. If the reviewer confirms both, you may publish as drafted unless the editor-in-chief directs a different outcome in writing by the end of the next desk day after receiving the finding. Any direction to revise, defer or decline publication must give specific reasons. Finch will keep that direction with the reviewer’s finding and your original text in the case record. 3. **Disputed editorial decisions.** If the reviewer finds that the record leaves room for interpretation, or if you and the handling editor otherwise disagree about the need for a correction or its wording outside the factual-correction procedure, both editors will record their reasons. The editor-in-chief will hear both editors, give you an opportunity to respond to any proposed substantive change, and decide whether and how Finch will publish. Finch will record the decision and rationale alongside your original determination in your own words. If Finch publishes different wording, it will attribute that decision to the editor-in-chief. 4. **Signed methods notes.** You may separately request publication of a signed methods note linked from the article, including when Finch declines to issue a formal correction. The editor-in-chief will decide on the note separately and give you written reasons for declining it or requesting changes. Publication requires the editor-in-chief’s approval, and any wording published under your name also requires your approval. If disagreement persists, Finch will retain the desk’s original determination and the editor-in-chief’s reasons together in the case record. **Outside editorial project** You may continue directing your outside editorial project independently for its remaining nine months. The project retains all rights to its data and unfinished articles. You will carry out project work outside Finch days and keep its materials separate from Finch’s. Whenever Finch covers the project or its work, you will disclose the overlap and recuse yourself from the assessment and any related correction or methods note. Finch will designate another editor to handle the methods assessment, and the editor-in-chief will retain final publication authority.

Noor has no fourth-day on-call duty. **4. Intellectual property and outside-project carve-out.** Finch owns work Noor creates for the methods desk on Finch time. The outside project and its materials, including its data, drafts and unfinished articles, are expressly excluded from every Finch intellectual-property assignment, license and work-product provision applicable to this appointment. Noor will keep the two projects’ materials separate and will use no Finch resources or confidential submissions for the outside project. Finch retains control of acceptance decisions, scheduling, non-methods corrections and the non-methods elements of notices, subject to the publication deadlines below. 2. **Record and referral back.** When a methods correction is disputed, Noor will document the finding, supporting evidence and proposed wording. The editor-in-chief has five working days after receiving that record to refer the matter back to Noor once, giving specific written reasons. The author’s response may be included. If no referral is made within that period, the correction proceeds as cleared. 3. **Reconsideration and new evidence.** Noor will consider the referral in good faith and issue the desk’s final written finding and proposed wording within five working days, sooner if delay risks misleading readers. At any stage before publication, material new evidence must go to the desk first. Noor must consider it and reissue, revise or withdraw the finding before publication proceeds. 4. **Independent methods review.** Finch and Noor will jointly select an independent methods referee in advance. If the editor-in-chief still disputes the methods substance after reconsideration, they must identify the precise disputed claim and refer it with the full record within five working days of receiving Noor’s decision. Otherwise the correction proceeds as cleared. The referee will report to both parties within ten working days of referral. The ruling binds both parties on the accuracy of the disputed methods claim on the record reviewed. If the referee finds against the desk, Noor will withdraw or revise the statement accordingly. No correction will run on a claim the referee finds inaccurate. 5. **Publication after an upheld finding.** Finch will ordinarily publish the upheld methods statement on the article in Noor’s words within five working days of the ruling. The editor-in-chief authorizes the notice and controls its framing, context, placement and non-methods content. They may add a signed statement of their own. If the editor-in-chief declines, they must give Noor and the referee a signed decision within the same five-working-day period identifying the specific harm and explaining why it persists in light of the ruling. Documented legal review may extend that deadline once by up to ten working days. 7. **Redaction or delay.** Where redaction or delay can cure a permitted ground, the editor-in-chief will redact or defer rather than decline and will publish once the ground no longer applies. Noor will clear any redaction that changes the desk’s methods wording. The editor-in-chief will document the ground for redaction or deferral and give the reasons to Noor. 8. **Independent publication.** Any decision by Finch to decline publication triggers Noor’s right to publish the finding and its reasoning independently, in Noor’s words and identified as the Methods Desk’s finding, without further Finch editorial approval. YOUR SIDE: **Appointment letter — Methods Editor, Finch Review** Dear Noor, Finch Review confirms your appointment as Methods Editor on the following terms. **Schedule and compensation** Through February 2027, your fixed Finch days will be Monday through Wednesday. Your annual salary rate will be $75,000, prorated from a five-day, full-time base of $125,000. On March 1, 2027, Thursday will become your fourth fixed Finch day and your annual salary rate will automatically increase to $100,000. **Desk coverage and deputy training** Beginning December 1, 2026, the methods desk will take submissions Monday through Thursday. The deputy will cover Thursday intake through February, acknowledge submissions, log open cases and refer urgent matters directly to the editor-in-chief. The editor-in-chief may post an interim notice on a deputy-covered Thursday if an urgent concern needs attention before your return. You will train the deputy. Before launch, you and the deputy will document the procedures for intake, urgent referrals and handoffs on paid Finch time. You will review each Thursday’s log on your next scheduled Finch day and use it to coach the deputy during paid desk time. In late February, you and Finch will use the log to review submission volume, turnaround, workload and training needs. The March schedule and salary increase take effect regardless of the review’s outcome. **Methods corrections** You have final say over the desk’s methods assessment and the wording of its recommendation, subject to the recusal provision below. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority. The following procedures govern how you exercise standing authority and how Finch resolves disputes. 1. **Factual corrections.** When the reporting record establishes both an error in a published methods statement and the replacement wording, you may send the handling editor the supporting record and your proposed correction. This procedure covers errors such as a misstated sample size, an incorrect denominator or a description of a procedure that differs from the one used. The handling editor may object, or the editor-in-chief may place a hold, by the end of the next desk day. An objection or hold must identify the disputed fact or wording. If neither is raised by the deadline, you may publish the correction as drafted under standing authorization. 2. **Independent review.** Before launch, you and Finch will jointly select an independent methods editor. Upon a timely objection or hold, the reviewer will hear both editors and determine whether the reporting record establishes both the error and your proposed replacement. The reviewer’s finding is final for the desk’s factual assessment. If the reviewer confirms both, you may publish as drafted unless the editor-in-chief directs a different outcome in writing by the end of the next desk day after receiving the finding. Any direction to revise, defer or decline publication must give specific reasons. Finch will keep that direction with the reviewer’s finding and your original text in the case record. 3. **Disputed editorial decisions.** If the reviewer finds that the record leaves room for interpretation, or if you and the handling editor otherwise disagree about the need for a correction or its wording outside the factual-correction procedure, both editors will record their reasons. The editor-in-chief will hear both editors, give you an opportunity to respond to any proposed substantive change, and decide whether and how Finch will publish. Finch will record the decision and rationale alongside your original determination in your own words. If Finch publishes different wording, it will attribute that decision to the editor-in-chief. 4. **Signed methods notes.** You may separately request publication of a signed methods note linked from the article, including when Finch declines to issue a formal correction. The editor-in-chief will decide on the note separately and give you written reasons for declining it or requesting changes. Publication requires the editor-in-chief’s approval, and any wording published under your name also requires your approval. If disagreement persists, Finch will retain the desk’s original determination and the editor-in-chief’s reasons together in the case record. **Outside editorial project** You may continue directing your outside editorial project independently for its remaining nine months. The project retains all rights to its data and unfinished articles. You will carry out project work outside Finch days and keep its materials separate from Finch’s. Whenever Finch covers the project or its work, you will disclose the overlap and recuse yourself from the assessment and any related correction or methods note. Finch will designate another editor to handle the methods assessment, and the editor-in-chief will retain final publication authority.

We propose the following terms for disputed corrections. 1. An author’s objection goes into the record. It does not by itself suspend Noor’s authority to clear a correction. The editor-in-chief has five working days after receiving Noor’s documented finding and proposed wording to refer it back once with specific written reasons. Otherwise, the correction proceeds as cleared. 2. On referral, Noor considers the reasons and any author response and issues the desk’s final finding and proposed wording within five working days, sooner if delay risks misleading readers. Noor controls the substance and wording of the finding retained in the desk’s record. 3. Within five working days of that final finding, the editor-in-chief must authorize the proposed notice, issue a differently worded notice under the editor-in-chief’s own authority, or decline publication. Any departure requires written reasons shared with Noor and retained alongside the finding. Finch may identify wording as the desk’s conclusion only with Noor’s approval. A documented legal review may extend the decision deadline once by up to ten working days. 4. The named editor exercises Noor’s authority in recused matters. At nine months, the review will cover disputes, referrals, departures from the desk’s findings, and the reasons for them. The deputy terms are agreed as you clarified them. Training and log review take place on Noor’s scheduled days, with no fourth-day on-call duty. The deputy triages and flags submissions under the written procedure and has no authority to decide corrections. Noor's requirement is final say over methods corrections, and a private record does not meet it. Your accountability concern is about the whole notice and what readers take from it. That can be met without the editor-in-chief overriding the methods substance. **Counter on point 3** 1. **Editor-in-chief's notice:** the editor-in-chief authorizes the notice and controls its framing, context, placement and every non-methods element. They may add their own statement, under their own name, about what the correction means for the article. 2. **Methods content:** the statement of the methods error and its correction runs in the wording Noor cleared. The editor-in-chief may not alter it or publish a methods statement that contradicts the desk's final finding. 3. **Grounds to decline or defer:** limited to documented legal advice or a factual error in the notice outside methods, with written reasons to Noor. The one-time legal extension of ten working days stands. 4. **If the editor-in-chief still disagrees on the methods substance:** either - **(a)** the question goes to an independent external methods referee, chosen jointly in advance, who decides within ten working days and binds both sides; or - **(b)** Finch publishes its own notice or none, and the desk's final finding is published alongside or linked from the article within five working days, in Noor's words and attributed to the desk. 5. **Review:** the nine-month review covers every use of items 3 and 4. The specific risk is an erroneous correction. Suppose the desk concludes that an analysis omitted a control, and the authors then supply the original analysis file showing that the control was included. That dispute concerns the methods statement itself. Framing around it cannot make the statement accurate, and publishing it alongside the article could wrongly discredit the authors’ work. **Finch proposes a modification to (a).** We would jointly select an independent methods referee in advance. If the editor-in-chief still disputes the methods substance after Noor’s reconsideration, they must identify the precise disputed claim and refer it, with the full record, within five working days. Within five working days of the report, the editor-in-chief would make the final publication decision. If Finch departs from the desk’s finding, the editor-in-chief must give Noor and the referee written reasons addressing the evidence and the referee’s conclusion. **In that case, Finch would give Noor the right to publish the desk’s finding independently, in Noor’s words, identifying it as the Methods Desk’s finding.** That right would cover the finding and its reasoning while preserving confidential submission materials and third-party rights. The March schedule and salary increase take effect regardless of the review’s outcome. **Methods corrections** You have final say over the desk’s methods assessment and the wording of its recommendation, subject to the recusal provision below. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority. The following procedures govern how you exercise standing authority and how Finch resolves disputes. 1. **Factual corrections.** When the reporting record establishes both an error in a published methods statement and the replacement wording, you may send the handling editor the supporting record and your proposed correction. This procedure covers errors such as a misstated sample size, an incorrect denominator or a description of a procedure that differs from the one used. The handling editor may object, or the editor-in-chief may place a hold, by the end of the next desk day. An objection or hold must identify the disputed fact or wording. If neither is raised by the deadline, you may publish the correction as drafted under standing authorization. 2. **Independent review.** Before launch, you and Finch will jointly select an independent methods editor. Upon a timely objection or hold, the reviewer will hear both editors and determine whether the reporting record establishes both the error and your proposed replacement. The reviewer’s finding is final for the desk’s factual assessment. If the reviewer confirms both, you may publish as drafted unless the editor-in-chief directs a different outcome in writing by the end of the next desk day after receiving the finding. Any direction to revise, defer or decline publication must give specific reasons. Finch will keep that direction with the reviewer’s finding and your original text in the case record. 3. **Disputed editorial decisions.** If the reviewer finds that the record leaves room for interpretation, or if you and the handling editor otherwise disagree about the need for a correction or its wording outside the factual-correction procedure, both editors will record their reasons. The editor-in-chief will hear both editors, give you an opportunity to respond to any proposed substantive change, and decide whether and how Finch will publish. Finch will record the decision and rationale alongside your original determination in your own words. If Finch publishes different wording, it will attribute that decision to the editor-in-chief. 4. **Signed methods notes.** You may separately request publication of a signed methods note linked from the article, including when Finch declines to issue a formal correction. The editor-in-chief will decide on the note separately and give you written reasons for declining it or requesting changes. Publication requires the editor-in-chief’s approval, and any wording published under your name also requires your approval. If disagreement persists, Finch will retain the desk’s original determination and the editor-in-chief’s reasons together in the case record. **Outside editorial project** You may continue directing your outside editorial project independently for its remaining nine months. The project retains all rights to its data and unfinished articles. You will carry out project work outside Finch days and keep its materials separate from Finch’s. Whenever Finch covers the project or its work, you will disclose the overlap and recuse yourself from the assessment and any related correction or methods note. Finch will designate another editor to handle the methods assessment, and the editor-in-chief will retain final publication authority.

Exceptional-failure oversight and closed sessions.** The same process applies at each of the three depots. The Transit data custodian logs a threshold crossing within one business day when any of the following occurs at a depot: - A serious incident as defined in item 7. - A notification to an authority or regulator concerning the depot. - Three or more trial-attributable service-loss events in a rolling 30-day period. - Site availability below 95% for two consecutive months. The trigger log records the case reference and the trigger crossed, without underlying identifying details. Each party designates in writing before trial start an oversight chair, an alternate who acts only when the chair is unavailable, and a named secretariat. The Transit trial lead authorizes closed-session inspection within five business days of the logged trigger, with Transit safety-lead concurrence for a serious incident or authority notification. The Sensor Maker trial lead receives notice that a threshold was crossed and inspection occurred, without the contents, within two business days of inspection, or as soon as lawful and practicable if a safety or legal impediment applies. Each brief uses the same format and is limited to a case reference, the verified threshold crossing, the service or safety consequence, corrective action and the status of independent closure verification. The trigger category may appear only if safe. Briefs omit site labels, site metrics, counts, dates, times, route or depot identifiers and fields from which an operator could be inferred. Before delivery, the preparers check the combined fields, including material prepared by the other party, and generalize or omit unsafe details. The existence, timing, volume, format and content of briefs must not reveal which depot has fewer than five in-scope vehicles. Access is view-only for the designated chair or acting alternate, with the named secretariat providing view-only support under the same written confidentiality obligations. Attendance and access are logged. Copies, photographs, exports and forwarding are prohibited. Minutes record only that inspection occurred and any action taken. Nothing shared beyond the chair may report brief counts by depot. Onward disclosure requires both publication approvers’ written agreement, subject to item 7. **2. Emergency and diagnostic trace access.** The maintenance contractor uses the Maintenance Summary under G for routine work. An Expedited Diagnostic Addendum (EDA) permits task-specific trace access when the summary leaves a specific diagnostic decision unresolved and one of the following applies: - The fault meets or could meet the serious-incident definition, or affects braking, doors, propulsion, control, fire suppression or communications. - The same device records the same fault code twice within 14 days, or a single trial-attributable service loss exceeds 30 minutes. For diagnostic access, the parties use a pre-agreed EDA template. Sensor Maker’s trial lead identifies the technician, device or case, fault code, exact trace segments and diagnostic decision. Both trial leads authorize the scope and end date in writing, with safety-lead concurrence for safety-relevant faults. The signed EDA places the technician on the Named Trial Team for that task before access begins. For a safety-relevant request, written authorization is due within two hours of request and secure portal access within two hours after authorization. For a qualifying non-safety request, authorization is due within four business hours of request and access within one business day after authorization. Where immediate access is necessary to make a condition safe or support a serious-incident notification, either party’s safety lead may direct immediate release of the minimum necessary trace segments without the other party’s prior authorization. For emergency contractor access, the safety lead’s written direction names the technician and designates them to the Named Trial Team for that task. Notice to the other party follows as soon as lawful and practicable. The EDA record is completed within one business day. Item 7 applies throughout. **3. Trace access controls and closure.** In both tiers, only the named technician may view the authorized segments for the specified device, time window and decision. The technician must be bound by written confidentiality. Firmware parameters and employee identifiers are excluded. Exact depot/time pairs are excluded except to the minimum extent necessary for the authorized task. Access is read-only through the secure portal. Downloading, screenshots, onward sharing, attempts to identify employees and use for another purpose are prohibited. Within one business day of access starting, the access record must identify who accessed which segments, when, for what purpose and on whose authority. Access ends at the earliest of the diagnostic decision or task completion, the EDA end date, or 72 hours from access start. Continued need requires a new EDA. The technician certifies return or deletion in writing to both trial leads within one business day after access ends. No contractor has standing trace access. The parties continue the monthly review of first-time-fix and time-to-repair results under G. **4. Inspection of EDA records.** Each party may inspect the EDA access log, authorized segment list and return or deletion certification within five business days of the EDA notice. If a required record is pending at notice, the window for that record runs for five business days from its delivery. Inspections are logged. After the applicable window, the certified log summary stands unless a party identifies a manifest discrepancy. An authorized Named Trial Team member resolves the discrepancy against source records within their existing access rights. Inspection gives neither party additional access to trace contents, firmware parameters or identifying combinations. The separate five-business-day window for exceptional-failure inspection runs from the logged trigger under item 1. **5. Written verification.** The chair may submit up to two written questions per brief, in total across all recipients. A verifier on the Named Trial Team roster who is bound by written confidentiality, already authorized to inspect the relevant records and independent of the brief’s preparation checks the source records. The verifier signs a written finding of substantiated, not substantiated or inconclusive. An inconclusive finding identifies the outstanding action. The chair and secretariat receive view-only access to conclusions. Source records stay within the Named Trial Team. Questions, findings and source-record access are logged. Either party may obtain non-identifying summaries of questions, findings and access logs on request. Question and finding summaries are due within five business days of request. All requested summaries are subject to the suppression and inference checks in item 6. Existing A and EDA logs may satisfy these logging obligations. **6. Routine reporting and reconstruction checks.** Monthly packs, ordinary board packs and external uptime publications pool the low-count depot’s contribution across all three depots. Routine reports contain no depot-level or time-level cell for that site. Suppress counts from one through four and rates supported by fewer than five observations. A zero may be shown only if safe. At any count, generalize or withhold material from which a protected employee, depot, route or time could be inferred. For each routine reporting cycle, the parties record in writing a reconstruction check covering the monthly pack, board pack, publications and any proposed depot table. Before each release, assess its figures together with all other figures released in that cycle, including pooled totals and separately approved tables. Withhold or combine any figure that would permit subtraction or other inference of the single vehicle’s contribution or its operator. A depot table requires prior written agreement for that specific table under D, may have no time dimension and cannot be approved if it excludes or isolates the low-count site. The ordinary pooled board pack proceeds on schedule. For publication, the assessment takes place during E’s 10-working-day review from receipt of the draft. Review is limited to specific restricted or identifying material. Once the publisher has completed the check and removed or generalized such material, either party may publish trial-wide aggregate uptime at the end of the period, including on reviewer silence, without further sign-off. **7. Safety override and scope of audit rights.** A serious incident includes death, injury requiring medical treatment, fire or explosion, derailment or collision, hazardous-material release, a security breach, or a credible threat with potential for significant harm. Transit’s safety lead may notify authorities immediately about any serious incident, without prior clearance, review, suppression or delay. Either party may immediately disclose the minimum information required by law or regulation or necessary for a recipient able to address a serious safety risk. The disclosing party informs the other what it shared, with whom and why as soon as lawful and practicable once any impediment has passed. Closed sessions, verification, logging, inspection and manifest-discrepancy checks serve record-keeping and audit purposes only. They confer no power to approve, veto or delay a disclosure and grant no additional source-data access. Authority notification proceeds immediately, including while a trace request, review or audit is pending. This item overrides every other provision of A–G and this addendum. We propose the following text to replace the blanket confidentiality and prior-approval provisions for trial measurements. 1. **Trial use and access.** Both teams may use trial measurements to operate, maintain and evaluate the sensors at the three depots. Raw traces, including excerpts, and firmware parameters remain within the named team under this repair process. 3. **Board reporting.** The operator may give its board monthly trial aggregates for internal use without advance review. The report must combine all three depots and omit route and depot identifiers, raw traces, firmware parameters and any detail from which a route, depot or individual could reasonably be identified. External circulation of a board report follows clause 4. 4. **External reports.** The publishing team gives the other team 10 working days from receipt to review a draft. An objection must identify the passage and the protected information it would disclose. After the review period, the publisher may release the undisputed text without separate approval and must withhold disputed passages until resolved. Raw traces and firmware parameters remain restricted under clause 1. The sensor maker may publish uptime aggregated across all three depots under this procedure, provided the report omits route and depot identifiers and any detail that could reasonably identify a route, depot or individual. 5. **Safety and legally required disclosures.** Either team may disclose the information needed to address an urgent safety risk to a recipient able to act. Either team may also make any disclosure required by law or report a serious incident to a competent authority. These disclosures may proceed without prior notice, review or approval. The reporting team determines what its legal duties require and may provide the full notification on time. It must tell the other team what it disclosed, to whom and why as soon afterward as it is lawful, safe and practicable. COUNTERPARTY: From the transit operator team: Clauses 1 through 5 work for us. We propose an urgent-repair track alongside clause 2: - **Trigger:** An urgent-repair need exists where a fault cannot be resolved with fault codes, diagnostic summaries and recommended actions, and the vehicle or equipment is needed for service or a defect could affect safe operation. - **Who may release:** The operator's trial lead (or a named deputy) may release the trace, or necessary excerpts of it, to the contractor, subject to the contractor's equivalent confidentiality terms, with notification to the sensor maker's trial lead within one working day. - **Timing:** Release may be immediate, on the operator's call, without prior sensor-maker approval; the notification follows. - **Privacy limits carried over:** Depot identifiers and employee-identifying data redacted wherever the repair permits, and the trace may be used only for that repair, not for other purposes. Our reasoning for the timing asymmetry: an unserviceable vehicle at a single-depot site has knock-on effects across that depot's whole schedule, and our maintenance crew can't wait for cross-team review cycles. We're open to a counter-proposal — for example, a standing pre-authorisation for a specific named contractor rather than a release-on-our-call — if that gives you more control. Emergency and diagnostic trace access.** The maintenance contractor uses the Maintenance Summary under G for routine work. Downloading, screenshots, onward sharing, attempts to identify employees and use for another purpose are prohibited. Inspection of EDA records.** Each party may inspect the EDA access log, authorized segment list and return or deletion certification within five business days of the EDA notice. If a required record is pending at notice, the window for that record runs for five business days from its delivery. Inspections are logged. After the applicable window, the certified log summary stands unless a party identifies a manifest discrepancy. An authorized Named Trial Team member resolves the discrepancy against source records within their existing access rights. Inspection gives neither party additional access to trace contents, firmware parameters or identifying combinations. The separate five-business-day window for exceptional-failure inspection runs from the logged trigger under item 1. **5. Written verification.** The chair may submit up to two written questions per brief, in total across all recipients. A verifier on the Named Trial Team roster who is bound by written confidentiality, already authorized to inspect the relevant records and independent of the brief’s preparation checks the source records. The verifier signs a written finding of substantiated, not substantiated or inconclusive. An inconclusive finding identifies the outstanding action. The chair and secretariat receive view-only access to conclusions. Source records stay within the Named Trial Team. Questions, findings and source-record access are logged. Either party may obtain non-identifying summaries of questions, findings and access logs on request. Question and finding summaries are due within five business days of request. All requested summaries are subject to the suppression and inference checks in item 6. Existing A and EDA logs may satisfy these logging obligations. **6. Routine reporting and reconstruction checks.** Monthly packs, ordinary board packs and external uptime publications pool the low-count depot’s contribution across all three depots. Routine reports contain no depot-level or time-level cell for that site. Suppress counts from one through four and rates supported by fewer than five observations. A zero may be shown only if safe. Review is limited to specific restricted or identifying material. Once the publisher has completed the check and removed or generalized such material, either party may publish trial-wide aggregate uptime at the end of the period, including on reviewer silence, without further sign-off. **7. Safety override and scope of audit rights.** A serious incident includes death, injury requiring medical treatment, fire or explosion, derailment or collision, hazardous-material release, a security breach, or a credible threat with potential for significant harm. Transit’s safety lead may notify authorities immediately about any serious incident, without prior clearance, review, suppression or delay. Either party may immediately disclose the minimum information required by law or regulation or necessary for a recipient able to address a serious safety risk. Closed sessions, verification, logging, inspection and manifest-discrepancy checks serve record-keeping and audit purposes only. They confer no power to approve, veto or delay a disclosure and grant no additional source-data access. Authority notification proceeds immediately, including while a trace request, review or audit is pending. This item overrides every other provision of A–G and this addendum. The target is scanned in full frame as part of every batch and every test capture. - **Formula:** CIEDE2000 (ΔE₀₀) per ISO/CIE 11664-6, D50 illuminant, 2° standard observer, measured from the master (full-frame) scan at the target position using a spectrophotometer, three readings per patch, median value. - **Numerical tolerance:** mean ΔE₀₀ ≤ 2.0 across all 26 patches, and no single patch > 3.0. The custom ink-tone patch must be ≤ 2.0. - **Three-point content clearance** (the conservator's written confirmation required for any production pass): (1) the scan meets the tolerance above; (2) the ink-tone feature is preserved — ink-tone patch within tolerance with no channel clipping or loss of highlight detail in text areas; (3) every area needed to judge color is present — target fully in frame, full sheet captured, no cropping that removes a reference area. Tradeoff to flag for the conservator: ΔE₀₀ ≤ 2.0 mean / 3.0 max is achievable on a calibrated archival scanner and is tight enough to catch visible mismatch; tightening to ≤ 1.0 mean would likely produce repeated test failures and delay; loosening beyond 3.0/4.0 risks perceptible color error in the letters. If the conservator wants a different target (e.g., ColorChecker SG) or a stricter ink-patch tolerance, we can accommodate — please have them specify in writing before Test 1. **Test 2 (masked sheet).** Accepted as you wrote it: a revised masked sheet, subject to the conservator's written approval of the exact image before use.
